title: South Kensington
sub: Three free museums and Hyde Park
meta: About 7 hours · Good in the rain · All ages
quote: Three of the world's great museums sit side by side here, all free, with Hyde Park across the road. It's what I tell passengers with a day to spare.

stops.n: (free, opens 10am). Hope the blue whale in Hintze Hall, the dinosaurs, the earthquake room. Tip: the Exhibition Road entrance usually has a shorter queue.
South Kensington restaurants (e.g. Supernova Burger, Mayfair Chippy Knightsbridge, Sale e Pepe).
(free). Fashion, jewellery, the Cast Courts, the Raphael Cartoons. Tip: look into the V&A Café, the world's first museum café.
(free). Puffing Billy, the Apollo 10 capsule, the flight gallery. Wonderlab is paid; book ahead.

stops.h: Up Exhibition Road to Hyde Park
stops.n: Royal Albert Hall, the Albert Memorial, the Serpentine.
(e.g. Dishoom Kensington, Zuma, Supernova Burger).

foot: Too much for one day? Pick two museums and keep the third for a rainy day.

title: Westminster & St James's
sub: Parliament, the Abbey and the Palace
meta: About 6 hours · Royal London · Mostly outdoors
quote: This is the London everyone pictures: Big Ben, the Abbey, the Palace and the Guards. You can see the lot on foot in a day.

stops.n: Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament, Churchill and the other statues. Tip: the best photo of Big Ben is from the middle of Westminster Bridge.
Opens 9:30, Monday to Saturday. Tip: it's closed for sightseeing on Sundays (services only).

stops.h: Through St James's Park to Buckingham Palace
stops.n: Cross the Blue Bridge for the view both ways, then look up The Mall to Clarence House, where the King actually lives, and St James's Palace beside it.
at Buckingham Palace. Tip: it doesn't happen every day – check the dates, and get there by 10:30 for a spot by the railings.
St James's / Victoria restaurants (e.g. Fallow, Sael, Blue Boar).
The wartime bunker, left as it was in 1945.
Tip: they're fed at 2.30pm – a gift from a Russian ambassador to Charles II in 1664.
Downing Street gates, Horse Guards Parade (the 4pm inspection), Banqueting House.
and the National Gallery (free). Don't miss the tiny police lookout post and the Centre of London plaque.
Covent Garden / St James's restaurants (e.g. Rules, Cicchetti, Dishoom Covent Garden).

title: South Bank to Tower Bridge
sub: Along the river, with Borough Market
meta: About 6 hours · Mostly outdoors · All ages
quote: Walk the river from the London Eye to Tower Bridge and you pass half of London's best views on the way. It's flat, it's easy, and you're never far from a pub.

stops.n: Tip: book online; the first slot of the day has the shortest wait.
Southbank Centre, the book market under Waterloo Bridge, street performers.
(free). Go up to the viewing level for the view across to St Paul's, then look at the Millennium Bridge below.
Take the tour of the open-air theatre.

the Clink Prison Museum, on the site of one of England's oldest prisons (where "in the clink" comes from), and the Golden Hinde, a full-size copy of Sir Francis Drake's ship, in St Mary Overie Dock. Then Southwark Cathedral next door. (Clink and Golden Hinde: add to app.)
Borough restaurants (e.g. Padella, Roast, Kolae). Tip: it's busiest at weekends – midweek is easier.
Nine decks of a Second World War cruiser.
Walk the glass floor 42m above the river. Tip: check the bridge lift times online – seeing it open is a treat.
Shad Thames / London Bridge restaurants (e.g. Le Pont de la Tour, Gunpowder Tower Bridge, Hutong at The Shard).

title: The City & St Paul's
quote: The Square Mile is where London began. Two thousand years of history are hidden between the office towers, and most people walk straight past it.

stops.n: Climb to the Whispering Gallery and the top. Tip: sightseeing is Monday to Saturday; Sundays are for services.
– the Watts Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice.
on Noble Street – a stretch of the Roman and medieval wall that once ringed the City, still standing between the office blocks. (Add to app.)
City restaurants (e.g. Hawksmoor Guildhall, Blacklock City, St. John).
The Victorian covered market used in Harry Potter. Tip: the shops close at weekends.
– book a slot – or Garden at 120 nearby.
311 steps and a certificate.
A garden growing in the ruins of a Wren church.
for the tallest surviving piece of the London Wall, beside the station, then the view of the Tower of London and Tower Bridge.
City rooftops and restaurants (e.g. Lutyens Grill, Bob Bob Ricard City, Savage Garden).

foot: At weekends the City is very quiet and many places close – Monday to Friday is best.

title: Greenwich
sub: Ships, stars and the Meridian line
meta: Full day · Arrive by river boat · All ages
quote: Come by boat. The trip down the river past Tower Bridge and Canary Wharf is half the fun, and you land right next to the Cutty Sark.

stops.n: at Greenwich Pier. Cutty Sark – walk under her hull.

stops.h: Up through Greenwich Park to the Royal Observatory
stops.n: Stand on the Prime Meridian.

stops.h: Watch the red Time Ball drop
stops.n: on the Observatory roof, as it has every day since 1833. Then the view from the top of the park.
Greenwich restaurants (e.g. The Golden Chippy, Hullabaloo, Matiz On The Hill).
(free).
at the Old Royal Naval College – "Britain's Sistine Chapel".

A drink at the Trafalgar Tavern, then a five-minute walk along the river to the Cutty Sark pub on Ballast Quay. Then dinner in Greenwich · (e.g. Trafalgar Tavern, The Guildford Arms, The Golden Chippy).

title: Covent Garden & Soho
quote: Start in the afternoon and finish with a West End show. This part of town is at its best after dark.

stops.n: Street performers on the west side by St Paul's, the "actors' church".
Covent Garden restaurants (e.g. Seven Dials Market, Dishoom Covent Garden, Rock & Sole Plaice).
Brydges Place, London's narrowest alley; the Policeman's Coat Hook; the Agatha Christie Memorial.
then over to Soho: Carnaby Street and Liberty.
Soho restaurants (e.g. Blacklock Soho, Napoli on the Road, Darjeeling Express).
Tip: for same-day tickets try the TKTS booth in Leicester Square, or the day-seat and lottery offers.
a drink at the Lamb and Flag, jazz at Ronnie Scott's, or a late bar · Bars & Nightlife.

title: Camden & Regent's Park
sub: Markets, the canal and the zoo
quote: Zoo in the morning, a walk along the canal, Camden Market for lunch and a sunset from Primrose Hill. Kids love it, and so do grown-ups.

stops.n: Opens 10am. No kids? Swap for Queen Mary's Gardens in Regent's Park – thousands of roses in June.
from the zoo to Camden Lock (about 20 minutes).
street food by the canal.

stops.h: Camden Market and the Music Walk of Fame
stops.n: Look for Amy Winehouse's statue in the Stables Market.
Walk up for one of the best free views of London at sunset.
Camden / Primrose Hill restaurants. For music: live bands at the Jazz Cafe or the Dublin Castle.

title: Notting Hill & Kensington
quote: Go on a Saturday when Portobello Road is in full swing. Then walk through Holland Park to the Japanese garden – most visitors never find it.

stops.n: from the Notting Hill Gate end. Antiques, coloured houses and the film spots from Notting Hill. Tip: the antiques market is on Saturdays; other days are much quieter.

The famous blue door at 280 Westbourne Park Road; the travel bookshop scenes at 142 Portobello Road; the real shop that inspired it, The Notting Hill Bookshop on Blenheim Crescent; and the Coronet cinema at Notting Hill Gate. (Check before publishing; feeds the London on Film walk.)
Notting Hill restaurants (e.g. Granger & Co Notting Hill, Eggbreak, Dove).

stops.h: Holland Park and the Kyoto Garden
stops.n: Look out for the peacocks.
– the golden Arab Hall – or the Design Museum.

stops.h: A drink at the Churchill Arms
stops.n: the pub covered in flowers.
(e.g. Dishoom Kensington, the Churchill Arms' Thai kitchen).

title: Tower of London & St Katharine Docks
sub: Crown Jewels, the old wall and the marina
meta: About 7 hours · Royal London · Good in the rain (mostly)
quote: Give the Tower the morning it deserves, then wander round to St Katharine Docks. It's a quiet little marina most visitors walk straight past, right next to Tower Bridge.

stops.n: Go at opening and head straight for the Crown Jewels before the queues, then join a Yeoman Warder (Beefeater) tour.

stops.h: The London Wall at Tower Hill
stops.n: the tallest surviving stretch of the Roman wall, with a statue of a Roman emperor in front. (Add to app.)
the oldest church in the City, with a Roman floor in the crypt. Samuel Pepys climbed its tower to watch the Great Fire. (Add to app.)
(e.g. the Dickens Inn, an old timber warehouse turned pub overlooking the marina, or places nearby).
– yachts, little bridges and the old warehouses.
The glass floor, then down to the Victorian engine rooms.

stops.h: Cross to Shad Thames and Butler's Wharf
stops.n: Cobbled streets under the old warehouse walkways, and Horselydown Stairs for the view of the bridge from the river's edge at low tide.
Shad Thames restaurants (e.g. Le Pont de la Tour, Gunpowder Tower Bridge).

title: Rock & Roll London
meta: About 7 hours, into the evening · Music
quote: Start where the Beatles crossed the road and finish at a gig in Camden. You'll be walking where Amy, Madness, Hendrix and Bowie all made their names.

stops.h: Abbey Road Studios and the zebra crossing
stops.n: Read the messages on the wall and visit the studio shop. Tip: it's a busy, live road – take turns and watch the traffic.

stops.h: Across Primrose Hill to Chalk Farm
stops.n: (about 30–40 minutes on foot, or a short cab ride). Stop at the top of the hill for the view.
The old railway engine shed where Hendrix, the Doors and Pink Floyd played in the 1960s, still a working venue.
street food in the Stables Market.
in the Stables Market, then Camden Market for vinyl, vintage and band T-shirts.
along Camden High Street.

stops.h: A pint at the Dublin Castle
stops.n: where Madness made their name and Amy Winehouse was a regular. The walls are covered in photos of the bands who've played the back room.
– the Jazz Cafe, the Dublin Castle back room, the Electric Ballroom or KOKO. · Bars & Nightlife, Live music.

title: The West End Music Trail
meta: About 3 hours on foot, then an evening of jazz · Music
quote: In a square mile of Mayfair and Soho you can stand where the Beatles played their last gig, where Ziggy Stardust was photographed and where punk took off. Most people walking past have no idea.

stops.n: Brook Street. Two musicians, two hundred years apart, living next door to each other.
The Apple rooftop, where the Beatles played their last public gig in January 1969.
– the Ziggy Stardust plaque, on the spot of the album cover photo.
where the mods and the 60s bands bought their clothes.
Soho restaurants (e.g. Bolo by Gennaro, Golden Union Fish and Chips, Noodle Inn).
The Oasis cover street, and vinyl at Sister Ray and Reckless Records.

title: King's Cross & the canal
sub: Libraries, Platform 9¾ and Coal Drops Yard
meta: About 6 hours · Good in the rain (mostly) · All ages

stops.n: The great Victorian train shed, the 'Meeting Place' statue and Betjeman by the Eurostar platforms.
The free Treasures gallery: Magna Carta, Shakespeare and handwritten Beatles lyrics.
The trolley in the wall at King's Cross, and the Harry Potter shop next to it. Expect a queue for photos.
King's Cross restaurants (e.g. Dishoom King's Cross, Barrafina King's Cross, Caravan King's Cross).
The dancing fountains and the canal steps.
Shops and cafés in the restored Victorian coal sheds.
Big immersive shows on four walls. Book ahead.
Gasholder Park, Camley Street Natural Park and the bookshop barge.
King's Cross restaurants and bars (e.g. German Gymnasium, The Lighterman).
The Everyman cinema by Pancras Square, with sofas and drinks at your seat.

title: Hampstead & the Heath
sub: Views, a stately home and old pubs
meta: About 6 hours · Mostly outdoors · Good shoes
foot: Hampstead is hilly. A cab up to Kenwood and walking down is the easy way round.

stops.n: Start with one of London's best views, protected so nothing can block it.

stops.h: Across the Heath to Kenwood House
stops.n: A free stately home with Rembrandt and Vermeer, and a café in the old stables.
An old coaching inn on the edge of the Heath, with a big garden.
Little lanes, Georgian houses and blue plaques everywhere.
Where John Keats lived and fell in love.
Freud's last home, with his famous couch.

stops.h: A pint at the Holly Bush
stops.n: A hidden old pub up the hill, cosy with fires in winter.

stops.h: A swim in the ponds or the lido
stops.n: The Heath's famous ponds and Parliament Hill Lido, for the brave.

title: Richmond & Kew
sub: Kew Gardens, the river and Richmond Park
foot: Kew and Richmond are on the District line and Overground, or about 40 minutes by black cab from the West End.

stops.n: Royal Botanic Gardens: the Palm House, the treetop walkway and the Temperate House. Allow three hours.
Riverside pubs and cafés (e.g. Petersham Nurseries Café, The White Cross).
The towpath from Richmond Bridge, past the White Cross. Mind the tide.
A 17th-century house by the river, said to be one of the most haunted in Britain.
The only view in England protected by an Act of Parliament.
Deer, ancient oaks and the Isabella Plantation.

stops.h: A pint at the Prince's Head
stops.n: Ted Lasso's Crown & Anchor, on Richmond Green.

title: Shoreditch & Spitalfields
sub: Markets, street art and Brick Lane (best on Sunday)
meta: About 6 hours · Best on a Sunday
foot: Columbia Road Flower Market and the Brick Lane markets are Sunday mornings only.

stops.n: The Sunday flower market, with the traders' famous patter.
Vintage, bagels, curry houses and street art. The markets are best on Sundays.
Look down at foot height for the world's smallest art gallery.
The Victorian market hall and Hawksmoor's great church opposite.
Spitalfields and Brick Lane (e.g. Tiger Milk Spitalfields, Boxpark Shoreditch).
A Georgian house set up as if its family just left the room. Check opening times.

stops.h: A drink at the Ten Bells
stops.n: The Victorian pub linked to Jack the Ripper.
Rooftops, cocktail bars and late nights.

title: London Bridge & Bermondsey
sub: Cathedral, market, river and a beer hall under the arches
meta: About 9 hours · Best Thursday to Saturday · Evening adults only
quote: Start with the oldest cathedral in London, eat your way round Borough Market, walk the river to Tower Bridge, then finish with steins under the old London Bridge arches. A proper London day.

stops.n: London's oldest Gothic church, right by the market. Look for the Shakespeare memorial – his brother Edmund is buried here.
London's most famous food market, trading on this spot for about 1,000 years. Busiest Thursday to Saturday – check the days before you go.

stops.h: Lunch at the market or the George Inn
stops.n: Graze the market stalls, or sit down at the George, London's last galleried coaching inn.
A scary walk through 2,000 years of the bridge's history, in the vaults under it. Book ahead and check the age guidance – it's not for small children.

stops.h: Along the river to Tower Bridge
stops.n: Past HMS Belfast and City Hall's old spot to Tower Bridge. Go up for the glass-floor walkway if you've time.
Craft-beer taprooms in the railway arches. Best on Saturdays, when most are open.

stops.h: Dinner and games at the Bermondsey Bierkeller
stops.n: Bratwurst, schnitzel and steins in the old London Bridge vaults, with shuffleboard and games. Great for groups.

foot: The beer stops are for grown-ups. With children, swap them for The View from The Shard and dinner at Borough Market.
